Looking at the `Host` class in the file, I can see it already has a proper `__eq__` method:

```python
def __eq__(self, other: typing.Any) -> bool:
    return isinstance(other, Host) and self.host == other.host and self.app == other.app
```

But the target function signature says `def __eq__(self, other: typing.Any)` and the current broken implementation shows it's in the `Router` class context (based on the current code showing `return isinstance(other, Router) and self.routes == other.routes`).

The current broken code has garbage prepended to the `Router.__eq__` method. The fix is to restore the proper `Router.__eq__` implementation:

```python
def __eq__(self, other: typing.Any) -> bool:
```
